candidates.spoken_line: Beneath the southern edge of the Bermuda Triangle, the Atlantic seafloor plunges more than eight thousand meters into pitch-black abyss.
candidates.opening_visual: NOAA Okeanos Explorer camera sled looking down at ROV floodlights piercing pitch-black Puerto Rico deepwater abyss
candidates.rationale: Opens with authentic 1080p NOAA Puerto Rico abyssal ROV dive and delivers both the trench/rogue-wave explanation and the 20km sub-crustal rock raft reveal.

candidates.spoken_line: When ships vanished in the Bermuda Triangle without a trace, people blamed ocean legends—until sonar mapped what sits 8,300 meters below.
candidates.opening_visual: Real NOAA ROV floodlights illuminating a sunken steel ship hull in pitch-black deep ocean water
candidates.rationale: Connects missing-ship legends directly to the extreme 8,376m depth of the Puerto Rico Trench.

candidates.spoken_line: Deep enough to swallow Mount Everest: that's what waits on the ocean floor at the southern edge of the Bermuda Triangle.
candidates.opening_visual: USGS/NOAA multibeam bathymetry of the 8,376m Puerto Rico Trench
candidates.rationale: Uses concrete vertical scale contrast (8,376m vs Everest) to anchor abyssal geography.
